Q: AX 2012 exception while adding inventory movement by C# WCF service A:

You're putting the wrong value in:

journalHeader.VoucherNumberSequenceTable

It ultimately contains the value from InventJournalName.VoucherNumberSequenceTable , which is a RecId (int64) corresponding to the number sequence.

You should check your relations or debug the InventDim portion.

Q: C/C++ standard string conversion functions don't support binary string literals? A:

Are there any standard C or C++ functions that will auto-detect a binary string, for example "0b1010" and convert it to integer 10?

In C, since C23, strtol(nptr, endptr, base), strtoll(nptr, endptr, base), strtol(nptr, endptr, base), strtoll(nptr, endptr, base) with base == 0 will auto-detect a binary string and convert as hoped.
When the base == 2, the "0b" or "0B" prefix is optional.

Also since C23, sscanf("%i", nptr), sscanf("%li", nptr), sscanf("%lli", nptr), (and a few others) will auto-detect a binary string and convert as hoped.

Prior to C23, hand-crafter code (or compiler extensions) were needed.

Q: QTableView does not show data from the Sqlite 3 table A:

That error usually just means Qt doesn’t have a database connection open.

QSqlQueryModel doesn’t open SQLite for you. If no QSqlDatabase is created and opened first, you’ll get “Driver not loaded”.

Before calling setQuery(), make sure you’ve done something like this:

from PySide6.QtSql import QSqlDatabase

self.db = QSqlDatabase.addDatabase("QSQLITE")
self.db.setDatabaseName("your_database.db")

if not self.db.open():
    print(self.db.lastError().text())

Then pass the connection to the model:

self.model = QSqlQueryModel(self)
self.model.setQuery(sql, self.db)

Also try:

print(QSqlDatabase.drivers())

If "QSQLITE" isn’t in the list, the SQLite plugin isn’t installed properly.

Q: .NET 10 version update generates BuildHost-net472 and BuildHost-netcore folder shortcuts A:

Upgrading "Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design" to version 10.0.2 or greater solves the issue. No need for workarounds.

Q: Jira /rest/raven/1.0/import/feature is creating new test although existing test is present in repo A:

Please check the global Xray's Miscellaneous settings in our Jira global settings (you'll need Jira administration rights for this or you can ask your Jira administrator). More precisely, check the "Cucumber Export Prefixes" settings. If your tests are exported with the "TEST_" prefix, then you must use them whenever adding tags to your scenarios So, if you have a Test with issue key ABCD-1987, and have the "TEST_" prefix, the tag you should add in your scenario should be @TEST_ABCD-1987.

One good way to indirectly check this setting, without bugging your Jira administrator, is to export the Test to Cucumber, from the Test issue screen and then see the generated .feature file. Then you can identify the Test prefix.

Q: Changes to --editable Python libraries require a reset of ipython to be seen A:

It looks like the root cause of the issue is that you have a from x import y statement. That is, when you invoke dummy.dummy_fct(), you are actually invoking a function that was defined in dummy.core.

If you do importlib.reload(dummy), then the dummy module will be reloaded, but it reuse the cached version of dummy.core. So it continues with the cached behaviour from before. Conversely, if you reload dummy.core, then although dummy.core will have the new value, the dummy module remains uneffected. For the reload to work as you desire, you must first reload dummy.core and then reload dummy. Example:

In [1]: import dummy

In [2]: dummy.dummy_fct()
Out[2]: True

In [3]: edit src/dummy/core.py
Editing... done. Executing edited code...

In [4]: import importlib

In [5]: importlib.reload(dummy)
Out[5]: <module 'dummy' from '/home/jackh/python/dummy/src/dummy/__init__.py'>

In [6]: dummy.dummy_fct()  # previous reload appears to have no effect
Out[6]: True

In [7]: importlib.reload(dummy.core)
Out[7]: <module 'dummy.core' from '/home/jackh/python/dummy/src/dummy/core.py'>

In [8]: dummy.dummy_fct()  # previous reload also appears to have no effect
Out[8]: True

In [9]: dummy.core.dummy_fct()  # however, a direct access shows that it has
Out[9]: False

In [10]: importlib.reload(dummy)
Out[10]: <module 'dummy' from '/home/jackh/python/dummy/src/dummy/__init__.py'>

In [11]: dummy.dummy_fct()  # final reload of dummy shows desired effect
Out[11]: False

Using autoreload 2 works because it reloads every module that has been imported. It also tries to be clever, by reloading child modules before parent modules.

If you just need to run an script that uses the effected library (as you state in your question), then you should consider running it in a fresh interpreter. That way you do not have to worry about caching issues. Examples:

In [1]: import dummy

In [2]: dummy.dummy_fct()
Out[2]: True

In [3]: edit src/dummy/core.py
Editing... done. Executing edited code...

In [4]: import sys

In [5]: !{sys.executable} -c 'import dummy; print(dummy.dummy_fct())'
False

In [6]: sys.executable
Out[6]: '/path/to/venv/bin/python3.14'

Use sys.executable to ensure that the subprocess uses the same virtual environment that your ipython is part of.
